# Adjudication Task — Chapter 645

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃645화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|누가 먼저 선을 넘었을까.
  6|
  7|나? 아니면 백상?
  8|
  9|그리고 나와 그가 나누었던 말 중, 무엇이 진실이며 거짓일까.
 10|
 11|짧은 순간 여러 가지 의문들이 뇌리를 스쳤지만 그런 건 이제 더 이상 중요하지 않았다.
 12|
 13|지금부터는 말과 생각이 아니라 오직 힘으로 결과를 논하는, 순수한 무림인들의 시간이니까.
 14|
 15|쉭!
 16|
 17|귓가를 파고드는 날카로운 파공성.
 18|
 19|소리를 듣기도 전에 고개를 꺾어 날아드는 지풍(指風)을 피해 낸 나는, 한 치의 망설임도 없이 앞에 놓인 석탁(石卓)을 짚었다.
 20|
 21|쿠웅!
 22|
 23|거대한 암석을 깎아 만든 탁자가 진동한다.
 24|
 25|동시에 튕겨지듯 허공으로 떠오르는 서른세 개의 술잔. 나는 부드럽게 손을 내뻗어 그중 일부를 밀어 냈다.
 26|
 27|퉁.
 28|
 29|오직 한 사람. 백상을 향해.
 30|
 31|쉬쉬쉬쉭!
 32|
 33|그것은 나무를 대충 다듬어 만든 투박한 술잔들에 불과했으나, 내가 흘려보낸 공력을 머금자 무시무시한 흉기로 돌변했다.
 34|
 35|화살보다 빠른 속도. 그리고 바위도 부술 만큼의 파괴력.
 36|
 37|하지만 상대는 침착했고, 침착하기 이전에 강했다.
 38|
 39|후웅, 서걱!
 40|
 41|곧게 편 수도(手刀)가 횡으로 휘둘려지자, 보이지 않는 무형의 기가 허공을 격하고 날아들던 술잔들을 갈랐다.
 42|
 43|그리고 힘을 잃은 채 산산조각이 난 술잔의 파편이 지면에 떨어지기도 전, 솟구치듯 자리에서 일어난 그의 신형이 흐릿해졌다.
 44|
 45|파팟!
 46|
 47|대전에 내려앉은 어둠 너머에서 새하얀 옷자락이 유령처럼 흩날린다.
 48|
 49|어느덧 석탁 위를 가로질러 오 장에 달하는 거리를 지워 버린 그가 앉아 있던 내 정수리를 향해 일권(一拳)을 내리찍으려던 그 순간.
 50|
 51|“선을 넘으시네, 또.”
 52|
 53|나는 낮은 뇌까림과 함께 손바닥을 쳐올리듯 내뻗었다.
 54|
 55|화륵.
 56|
 57|화염신장(火焰神掌).
 58|
 59|어둠을 살라 먹으며 타오른 화염이, 눈부신 강기가 서린 백상의 일권과 맞닿는다.
 60|
 61|각각 희고 푸른 기운이 뒤섞이며 터져 나온 섬광이 사방을 뒤흔들었다.
 62|
 63|콰앙! 구구궁!
 64|
 65|내리꽂히는 일권과 쳐올리는 일장. 노인과 청년. 원초적이며 순수한 힘의 충돌.
 66|
 67|거센 진동과 굉음이 대전을 뒤흔들었고, 나는 똑똑히 볼 수 있었다.
 68|
 69|화아아악!
 70|
 71|맞닿은 일점(一點)을 중심으로 폭발하듯 흘러나온 광휘 너머, 크게 뜨인 한 쌍의 눈동자를.
 72|
 73|“……!”
 74|
 75|언제나 서늘한 빛을 발하던 백상의 눈동자에는 감출 수 없는 놀라움이 서려 있었다.
 76|
 77|어떻게?
 78|
 79|낯익은 감정. 익숙한 눈빛이다.
 80|
 81|지금까지 나와 마주친 이들 중 대부분이 마찬가지였으니까.
 82|
 83|그들은 내 이름과 별호가 무림에 알려지기 시작한 이전에도, 그리고 이후에도 간혹 그 사실을 망각한 듯 때 이른 과소평가를 내리고는 했다.
 84|
 85|나이가 어려서. 출신 가문이 한미해서. 혹은 전란(戰亂)을 겪어 보지 못한 애송이라서.
 86|
 87|그리고 그런 일이 생길 때마다 나는 친절하게 알려 주었다.
 88|
 89|말이 아닌 힘으로.
 90|
 91|‘바로 지금처럼.’
 92|
 93|입 밖으로 새어 나가지 않은 뇌까림과 함께, 나는 전신에 충만한 기운을 한층 더 강하게 끌어올렸다.
 94|
 95|콰아아아!
 96|
 97|자그마치 삼 갑자에 달하는 강대한 공력이 기지개를 켜며 일어난다.
 98|
 99|열양지기가 뿜어내는 끔찍한 열기에 주위의 수분이 증발하고 붉은 아지랑이가 피어올랐다.
100|
101|츠츠츠츠!
102|
103|활짝 펼친 손바닥에 가로막혀 있던 주먹이 서서히 밀려 나가기 시작했다.
104|
105|파르르 떨리는 백상의 눈동자에, 타들어 가는 그의 새하얀 옷자락과 담담한 내 얼굴이 차례대로 스친다.
106|
107|열기에 쩍쩍 갈라진 백상의 입술 사이로 서늘한 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
108|
109|“네놈…….”
110|
111|대단한 평정심이다. 보통 이런 상황에서 내가 들었던 말 중 대부분은 씨발놈, 개새끼, 미친놈이었으니까.
112|
113|그러나 백전(百戰)을 치르며 단련된 것일까. 아니면 수만의 부족민을 이끄는 대족장이기 때문일까.
114|
115|백상의 감정은 출렁일지언정 흘러넘치지 않았고, 그의 무위는 내가 생각한 것 이상으로 뛰어났다.
116|
117|스슥!
118|
119|까맣게 타들어 간 옷깃이 팔뚝을 스친다. 어느새 굳게 말아쥐고 있던 주먹이, 매의 발톱처럼 펼쳐져 섬광 같은 속도로 내 손목을 움켜쥐었다.
120|
121|아니, 아마도 틀림없이 움켜쥐었을 것이다.
122|
123|내 움직임이 그보다 더 빠르고, 강하지 않았다면.
124|
125|콰득!
126|
127|이미 인간의 한계를 아득히 벗어난 힘.
128|
129|무시무시한 악력으로 손목을 조이자, 고통을 느낀 백상의 눈썹이 움찔 떨리며 짧은 신음이 튀어나왔다.
130|
131|“흡!”
132|
133|그리고 나는 그 찰나의 빈틈을 놓치지 않았다.
134|
135|‘지금.’
136|
137|백상의 손목을 옆으로 틀어 다른 한 손을 봉함과 동시에 중심을 흐트린 다음, 남은 한 손으로 옆구리를 향해 일장(一掌).
138|
139|퍼엉!
140|
141|나는 둔중한 파공음이 들리기도 전에 그의 손목을 놔주었다.
142|
143|수십여 쌍의 시선이 지켜보는 앞에서, 옆구리를 후려친 장력에 의해 튕겨 나간 백상이 허공에서 몸을 틀어 석탁 위에 내려앉았다.
144|
145|슥.
146|
147|소리도 나지 않을 만큼 가벼운 몸놀림이었지만 표정은 정반대다.
148|
149|그리고 무겁게 가라앉은 눈빛으로 나를 노려보던 백상이 재차 움직이려던 그때.
150|
151|“그만.”
152|
153|목소리는 크지 않았지만, 깊은 울림과 위엄이 담겨 있었다. 어느덧 자리에서 일어난 야수묘왕이 굳은 얼굴로 입을 열었다.
154|
155|“물러서라. 두 사람 모두.”
156|
157|백상의 신형이 흔들렸고, 나는 어깨를 으쓱해 보였다.
158|
159|“전 안 움직였는데요.”
160|
161|틀림없는 사실이다. 비록 의자를 좀 뒤로 빼긴 했지만, 먼저 쇄도한 것은 백상이었고 나는 앉은 채로 수를 주고받았을 뿐이었다.
162|
163|그리고 결과는, 뭐.
164|
165|귀신에 홀린 듯한 눈으로 나를 바라보는 다른 부족장들의 눈빛이 그 증거고 결과다.
166|
167|“진태경.”
168|
169|하지만 최소한의 처신 정도는 해야 했다. 이곳은 내 홈그라운드가 아닌 남만이고, 상대는 백족의 대족장이었으니까.
170|
171|야수묘왕의 질책 어린 부름에 나는 양손을 들어 보였다.
172|
173|“죄송합니다. 손을 쓰지 않을 수가 없던 상황이라 저도 모르게 그만.”
174|
175|물론 그래도 짚고 넘어가긴 해야지.
176|
177|백번 양보해서 문제의 발단은 나였을지 몰라도, 백상이 펼친 수는 자칫하면 절명에 이를 수 있는 위험한 공격이었다.
178|
179|“……후우.”
180|
181|내 말뜻을 알아들었는지, 나직한 한숨을 내쉰 야수묘왕의 시선이 다른 한 사람을 향해 움직였다.
182|
183|“백상, 경거망동하지 말거라.”
184|
185|차가운 눈동자에 갈등이 스친다.
186|
187|등 뒤에서 들려온 야수묘왕의 부름에도 아무런 대답 없이 나를 응시하던 백상이 문득 주위를 둘러봤다.
188|
189|서른 명이 넘는 부족장들.
190|
191|그들의 반응은 세 갈래로 나뉘었다. 당장이라도 내게 달려들 것처럼 엉덩이를 들썩이는 이도 있었고, 웃음을 참는 듯 입가를 씰룩이는 자도 있었으며, 내 무위를 목격하고 반쯤 넋이 나간 이들도 있었다.
192|
193|이건 남만야수궁 내에서 파벌이 존재한다는 증거였다.
194|
195|그리고 모두가 지켜보는 앞에서 백상의 위상과 명성에는 쉽게 지울 수 없는 흠집이 새겨졌다.
196|
197|다른 누구도 아닌, 바로 중원에서 온 한족 애송이에 의해서.
198|
199|“…….”
200|
201|그런 사실을 모를 리가 없는 백상이다. 입술을 지그시 깨문 그는 야수묘왕을 향해 고개를 숙였다. 억눌린 목소리와 함께.
202|
203|“분란을 일으켜 송구합니다. 마음을 가라앉힌 후 다시 뵙지요.”
204|
205|그리고는 곧장 까맣게 그을린 옷자락을 펄럭이며 대전을 빠져나갔다.
206|
207|동시에 자연스럽게 일어난 요희가 그 뒤를 따랐고, 허둥지둥 움직이는 흑웅과 절반에 달하는 부족장들 역시 눈치를 살피며 자리에서 일어났다.
208|
209|“궁주님, 송구하지만 그럼…….”
210|
211|“가, 같이 갑시다.”
212|
213|저들이 친(親) 백상파로 분류되는 이들일 것이다. 평범한 온건파와는 달리 무림맹 입맹을 결사반대하는 자들.
214|
215|서른두 명의 부족장 중 대략 절반에 달하는 이들이 그렇게 자리를 비우자, 야율목은 분노로 미간을 찌푸렸고 야수묘왕은 피곤한 목소리로 중얼거렸다.
216|
217|“결국 이 사달이 났군.”
218|
219|내가 눈치를 살피며 입을 열었다.
220|
221|“죄송합니다. 괜히 저 때문에 벌어진 일 같네요.”
222|
223|“후우, 네가 사과할 일이 아니다. 언제고 터질 문제였지.”
224|
225|“아하, 그럼 다행이고요. 사실 저도 그렇게 생각하긴 했습니다.”
226|
227|“…….”
228|
229|그 순간. 아직 남아 있던 부족장들은 물론이고 야율목과 야수묘왕까지 짜게 식은 눈빛으로 나를 바라봤다.
230|
231|- 너 때문인 거 맞아. 이 새끼야.
232|
233|뭐지, 환청인가? 분명히 전음은 아닌데.
234|
235|희한한 현상에 고개를 갸웃거린 내가 재차 입을 열었다.
236|
237|“혹시 대회의가 이대로 끝난 건 아니죠?”
238|
239|“대회의는 축제와 더불어 사흘간 진행된다. 참석 전에 이미 들었을 텐데?”
240|
241|“듣긴 했는데 혹시나 해서.”
242|
243|내 천연덕스러운 대답에 야수묘왕이 고개를 절레절레 내저었다.
244|
245|“꼭 그렇게까지 해야 했느냐?”
246|
247|“그래도 지나치기에는 너무 찜찜했습니다. 진짜 반응도 궁금했고요.”
248|
249|“그 호기심 때문에 넌 일만이 넘는 백족을 적으로 만들었다. 백상을 따르는 요희와 흑웅. 두 대족장과 다른 이들까지 합하면 남만의 절반이라고 해도 과언이 아니겠지.”
250|
251|음. 남만의 절반이라.
252|
253|“생각보다는 나쁘지 않네요.”
254|
255|“뭐라?”
256|
257|“한 이틀 전만 해도 남만 전체가 제 적이었거든요. 대회의는 뭐, 시작도 전에 쫓겨날 판이었고.”
258|
259|“……허. 참.”
260|
261|헛웃음을 흘린 야수묘왕이 남아 있던 부족장들에게 시선을 옮겼다.
262|
263|“장 족장. 그리고 고 족장.”
264|
265|“예.”
266|
267|“이번에는 그대들이 도와줘야겠다. 우선은 발 빠른 전사들로 척후대를 꾸리고, 귀주 방면 쪽을 감시하도록.”
268|
269|“혈승(血僧)이라는 자 때문입니까?”
270|
271|고개를 끄덕인 야수묘왕이 재차 입을 열었다.
272|
273|“백상과 진태경의 의견 모두 일리가 있다. 놈이 구태여 남만으로 향할 이유도 없지만, 암천의 인물이라면 그에 따른 대비를 해야 옳겠지.”
274|
275|“궁주님의 명을 따르겠습니다.”
276|
277|“존명.”
278|
279|앞서 떠난 부족장들이 백상에게 속해 있다면, 남은 이들 중 대부분은 야수묘왕에게 충성을 바치거나 상당히 호의적인 중도파다.
280|

Flames consumed the darkness and met Baeksang’s fist, which blazed with Force. White and blue energies mingled, bursting into a flash that shook the hall.

[P24]
*Boom! Rumble-rumble!*

[P25]
A descending fist and an upward palm. An old man and a young man. A collision of raw strength.

[P26]
The impact rocked the hall, and beyond the light exploding from the point where our attacks met, I saw Baeksang’s eyes widen.

[P27]
“…!”

[P28]
Those cold eyes held unmistakable surprise.

[P29]
*How?*

[P30]
I knew the look. Most of the people I’d faced had worn it.

[P31]
Even after my name and sobriquet became known throughout Murim, people sometimes seemed to forget and underestimated me. I was too young. My family was too humble. I was a green kid who had never been through a war.

[P32]
Whenever that happened, I kindly set them straight.

[P33]
Not with words.

[P34]
*Just like now.*

[P35]
I drew more of the energy filling my body to the surface.

[P36]
*Whoooosh!*

[P37]
Three jiazi of internal energy stirred to life. The terrible heat of my Scorching Yang Qi evaporated the moisture around us, and red heat haze rose into the air.

[P38]
*Tsss-tsss-tsss!*

[P39]
Baeksang’s fist began to give way against my open palm. His trembling eyes flicked from the white fabric burning at his sleeve to my calm face.

[P40]
A cool voice emerged from between his heat-cracked lips.

[P41]
“You bastard…”

[P42]
Remarkable composure. Usually, people in his position went straight to *fucking bastard*, *son of a bitch*, or *crazy bastard*.

[P43]
Maybe a hundred battles had tempered him. Maybe it came from leading tens of thousands of tribespeople. Whatever the reason, Baeksang kept his emotions in check. His martial prowess was greater than I’d expected, too.

[P44]
*Swish!*

[P45]
His blackened sleeve brushed my forearm. The fist he’d held clenched opened like a hawk’s talons and shot toward my wrist.

[P46]
It would have caught me, too, if I hadn’t moved faster and hit harder.

[P47]
*Crack!*

[P48]
I caught his wrist instead and squeezed with strength far beyond human limits. Pain made his brow twitch, and a short groan escaped him.

[P49]
“Hng!”

[P50]
I seized the opening.

[P51]
*Now.*

[P52]
I twisted his wrist aside, blocking his other hand and throwing him off balance. Then I drove my free palm into his flank.

[P53]
*Bang!*

[P54]
I released his wrist before the heavy report of the strike reached my ears.

[P55]
In front of dozens of watching chieftains, Baeksang flew backward. He twisted in midair and landed on the stone table.

[P56]
*Swish.*

[P57]
He touched down so lightly he made no sound. His expression was anything but light.

[P58]
He fixed me with a heavy stare and started to move again.

[P59]
“Enough.”

[P60]
The voice was quiet but resonant, carrying unmistakable authority. The Beast Miao King had risen from his seat.

[P61]
“Stand down. Both of you.”

[P62]
Baeksang’s figure wavered. I shrugged.

[P63]
“I didn’t move.”

[P64]
It was true. I’d slid my chair back a little, but Baeksang had charged at me. I’d exchanged blows with him without leaving my seat.

[P65]
And the result? Well, the other chieftains were staring at me as if they’d seen a ghost. Their faces said it all.

[P66]
“Jin Taekyung.”

[P67]
I did need to show some propriety. This was Nanman, not my home ground, and Baeksang was the great chieftain of the Bai people.

[P68]
At the Beast Miao King’s reproachful call, I raised both hands.

[P69]
“I’m sorry. I had to defend myself. I acted without thinking.”

[P70]
I still needed to make that clear. Even if I conceded that I’d started the trouble, Baeksang had used an attack that could have killed me.

[P71]
“…Hoo.”

[P72]
Perhaps he understood. The Beast Miao King sighed softly and turned to the other man.

[P73]
“Baeksang, do not act rashly.”

[P74]
Conflict flickered through Baeksang’s cold eyes. He kept staring at me without answering the Beast Miao King behind him, then looked around the hall.

[P75]
More than thirty chieftains watched us. Some shifted in their seats as if ready to rush me. Others fought back smiles. Still others looked half dazed by what they’d just seen.

[P76]
There were factions within the Nanman Beast Palace. And in front of all of them, Baeksang’s standing and Fame had taken a blow that would not be easily erased.

[P77]
At the hands of a Han Chinese brat from the Central Plains, no less.

[P78]
“…”

[P79]
Baeksang knew it. He pressed his lips together and bowed his head to the Beast Miao King.

[P80]
“I apologize for causing a disturbance. I will return once I have calmed myself.”

[P81]
Then he left the hall, his scorched robes fluttering behind him.

[P82]
Yohi rose and followed as if it were the most natural thing in the world. Heugung hurried after them, and nearly half the chieftains got up as well, watching one another for cues.

[P83]
“Palace Lord, forgive me, but I…”

[P84]
“L-let’s go together.”

[P85]
They were probably the pro-Baeksang faction. Unlike the ordinary moderates, they were fiercely opposed to Nanman joining the Murim Alliance.

[P86]
As roughly half of the thirty-two chieftains filed out, Yayul Mok frowned in anger. The Beast Miao King spoke wearily.

[P87]
“So it’s finally come to this.”

[P88]
I glanced at him before speaking.

[P89]
“I’m sorry. Feels like this happened because of me.”

[P90]
“Hoo. You have nothing to apologize for. It was bound to happen sooner or later.”

[P91]
“Oh, good. That’s what I thought, too.”

[P92]
“…”

[P93]
The remaining chieftains, Yayul Mok, and the Beast Miao King all gave me the same flat look.

[P94]
—It *is* because of you, you bastard.

[P95]
*What was that? I must be hearing things. It definitely wasn’t Sound Transmission.*

[P96]
I tilted my head at the strange phenomenon, then asked, “The grand council isn’t over, is it?”

[P97]
“The grand council runs for three days, alongside the festival. You were told that before you attended.”

[P98]
“I was. Just checking.”

[P99]
The Beast Miao King shook his head at my shameless answer.

[P100]
“Did you really have to take it that far?”

[P101]
“It felt too suspicious to let it go. I wanted to see his real reaction, too.”

[P102]
“That curiosity has made enemies of more than ten thousand Bai people. Add Yohi and Heugung, the two great chieftains who follow Baeksang, and the others, and it would be no exaggeration to say that half of Nanman is against you.”

[P103]
*Hmm. Half of Nanman.*

[P104]
“That’s not as bad as I expected.”

[P105]
“What?”

[P106]
“Two days ago, all of Nanman was against me. I was about to get thrown out before the grand council even started.”

[P107]
“…Hah.”

[P108]
The Beast Miao King gave a hollow laugh and turned to the chieftains who remained.

[P109]
“Chief Jang. Chief Go.”

[P110]
“Yes.”

[P111]
“I need your help. Gather a scouting party of swift warriors and have them watch the approaches from Guizhou.”

[P112]
“Because of the Blood Monk?”

[P113]
The Beast Miao King nodded.

[P114]
“Both Baeksang and Jin Taekyung have a point. The man has no particular reason to come to Nanman. But if he belongs to Dark Heaven, we should be prepared.”

[P115]
“We will obey your command, Palace Lord.”

[P116]
“As you command.”

[P117]
If the chieftains who had left were Baeksang’s people, most of those still here were loyal to the Beast Miao King or were moderates favorably disposed toward him.

[P118]
The two chiefs, each the leader of a mid-sized tribe, accepted their orders without protest. The Beast Miao King’s expression eased a little.

[P119]
“Tonight, we will erect a memorial for those who died and hold a banquet in their honor. The grand council will resume afterward. You may withdraw for now.”

[P120]
* * *

[P121]
“What happened?”

[P122]
Namho came rushing over the moment we returned to our quarters.

[P123]
“You didn’t cause another incident, did you?”

[P124]
His voice brimmed with suspicion. I was about to answer when Hyuk Mujin burst out indignantly.

[P125]
“Old man Nam! What do you take our Captain for?”

[P126]
“What else? A lunatic.”

[P127]
“Now, now. Even if our Captain *is* a lunatic, that’s going too far! Do you seriously think he’d cause trouble at a meeting that important?”

[P128]
“Yes. Easily.”

[P129]
*Is it normal to feel guilty right now?*

[P130]
I hesitated, then opened my mouth. Or tried to.

[P131]
That was when Ju Hwaran joined in.

[P132]
“Elder Namho, that’s too harsh. How can you call our Pavilion Master a lunatic?”

[P133]
If Taishan was the reason Namho was aging so quickly, Ju Hwaran was his one weakness. The man who had been so sure of himself a moment ago scratched his thinning crown.

[P134]
“Well, I…”

[P135]
“Our Pavilion Master came here representing the Murim Alliance. He can be a little rough around the edges, but he knows how important it is to secure Nanman’s entry into the alliance. He would never cause a disturbance at the grand council.”

[P136]
“…”

[P137]
*Please kill me.*

[P138]
My conscience had gone past pricking me. It hurt.

[P139]
Meanwhile, Ju Hwaran was canvassing the others like an enthusiastic campaigner.

[P140]
“What do you all think? Why isn’t anyone answering?”

[P141]
The usually quiet Song Ilseom smacked his lips.

[P142]
“Hmm. Young Bureau Head, perhaps we ought to hear from the man himself first…”

[P143]
“Extra bonus.”

[P144]
“On second thought, you’re right. The Pavilion Master would never do such a thing.”

[P145]
*Money-crazed bastard—out.*

[P146]
“Why aren’t the other two saying anything?”

[P147]
“Taishan. Hungry…”

[P148]
“I heard there’s a banquet tonight.”

[P149]
“Taishan. Strongly agrees with Young Lady Ju.”

[P150]
“…I agree as well.”

[P151]
*Glutton—out. Ex-fiancé I could chew to bits and still not feel satisfied—out.*

[P152]
Her petition gathered signatures with the speed of Quick Attack. Then Ju Hwaran turned eyes sparkling like the Milky Way on me.

[P153]
“Pavilion Master, say something. Did they agree to join the alliance?”

[P154]
One second felt like an hour.

[P155]
After a long silence, I spoke.

[P156]
“Um. Everyone. Well. There was… a minor problem.”

[P157]
Ju Hwaran froze. Namho nodded as if he’d known all along.

[P158]
“See? Crazy Pavilion Master.”

[P159]
“…”

[P160]
“Did you kill someone?”

[P161]
“No.”

[P162]
“Then you hit someone.”

[P163]
“…”

[P164]
“Who? Some chieftain who picked a fight without knowing better? Or someone who said something you didn’t like? Surely not the great chieftain of the Bai people.”

[P165]
“Ah.”

[P166]
“Pavilion Master?”

[P167]
“…”

[P168]
“…Pavilion Master?”

[P169]
As Ju Hwaran’s voice grew faint, I kept my mouth shut and stared toward a distant mountain.

[P170]
Namho chuckled.

[P171]
“See? Crazy bastard.”

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.

- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. ### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

*Just like now.*

[P35]
I drew more of the energy filling my body to the surface.

[P36]
*Whoooosh!*

[P37]
Three jiazi of internal energy stirred to life. The terrible heat of my Scorching Yang Qi evaporated the moisture around us, and red heat haze rose into the air.

[P38]
*Tsss-tsss-tsss!*

[P39]
Baeksang’s fist began to give way against my open palm. His trembling eyes flicked from the white fabric burning at his sleeve to my calm face.

[P40]
A cool voice emerged from between his heat-cracked lips.

[P41]
“You bastard…”

[P42]
Remarkable composure. Usually, people in his position went straight to *fucking bastard*, *son of a bitch*, or *crazy bastard*.

[P43]
Maybe a hundred battles had tempered him. Maybe it came from leading tens of thousands of tribespeople. Whatever the reason, Baeksang kept his emotions in check. His martial prowess was greater than I’d expected, too.

[P44]
*Swish!*

[P45]
His blackened sleeve brushed my forearm. The fist he’d held clenched opened like a hawk’s talons and shot toward my wrist.

[P46]
It would have caught me, too, if I hadn’t moved faster and hit harder.

[P47]
*Crack!*

[P48]
I caught his wrist instead and squeezed with strength far beyond human limits. Pain made his brow twitch, and a short groan escaped him.

[P49]
“Hng!”

[P50]
I seized the opening.

[P51]
*Now.*

[P52]
I twisted his wrist aside, blocking his other hand and throwing him off balance. Then I drove my free palm into his flank.

[P53]
*Bang!*

[P54]
I released his wrist before the heavy report of the strike reached my ears.

[P55]
In front of dozens of watching chieftains, Baeksang flew backward. He twisted in midair and landed on the stone table.

[P56]
*Swish.*

[P57]
He touched down so lightly he made no sound. His expression was anything but light.

[P58]
He fixed me with a heavy stare and started to move again.

[P59]
“Enough.”

[P60]
The voice was quiet but resonant, carrying unmistakable authority. The Beast Miao King had risen from his seat.

[P61]
“Stand down. Both of you.”

[P62]
Baeksang’s figure wavered. I shrugged.

[P63]
“I didn’t move.”

[P64]
It was true. I’d slid my chair back a little, but Baeksang had charged at me. I’d exchanged blows with him without leaving my seat.

[P65]
And the result? Well, the other chieftains were staring at me as if they’d seen a ghost. Their faces said it all.

[P66]
“Jin Taekyung.”

[P67]
I did need to show some propriety. This was Nanman, not my home ground, and Baeksang was the great chieftain of the Bai people.

[P68]
At the Beast Miao King’s reproachful call, I raised both hands.

[P69]
“I’m sorry. I had to defend myself. I acted without thinking.”

[P70]
I still needed to make that clear. Even if I conceded that I’d started the trouble, Baeksang had used an attack that could have killed me.

[P71]
“…Hoo.”

[P72]
Perhaps he understood. The Beast Miao King sighed softly and turned to the other man.

[P73]
“Baeksang, do not act rashly.”

[P74]
Conflict flickered through Baeksang’s cold eyes. He kept staring at me without answering the Beast Miao King behind him, then looked around the hall.

[P75]
More than thirty chieftains watched us. Some shifted in their seats as if ready to rush me. Others fought back smiles. Still others looked half dazed by what they’d just seen.

[P76]
There were factions within the Nanman Beast Palace. And in front of all of them, Baeksang’s standing and Fame had taken a blow that would not be easily erased.

[P77]
At the hands of a Han Chinese brat from the Central Plains, no less.

[P78]
“…”

[P79]
Baeksang knew it. He pressed his lips together and bowed his head to the Beast Miao King.

[P80]
“I apologize for causing a disturbance. I will return once I have calmed myself.”

[P81]
Then he left the hall, his scorched robes fluttering behind him.

[P82]
Yohi rose and followed as if it were the most natural thing in the world. Heugung hurried after them, and nearly half the chieftains got up as well, watching one another for cues.

[P83]
“Palace Lord, forgive me, but I…”

[P84]
“L-let’s go together.”

[P85]
They were probably the pro-Baeksang faction. Unlike the ordinary moderates, they were fiercely opposed to Nanman joining the Murim Alliance.

[P86]
As roughly half of the thirty-two chieftains filed out, Yayul Mok frowned in anger. The Beast Miao King spoke wearily.

[P87]
“So it’s finally come to this.”

[P88]
I glanced at him before speaking.

[P89]
“I’m sorry. Feels like this happened because of me.”

[P90]
“Hoo. You have nothing to apologize for. It was bound to happen sooner or later.”

[P91]
“Oh, good. That’s what I thought, too.”

[P92]
“…”

[P93]
The remaining chieftains, Yayul Mok, and the Beast Miao King all gave me the same flat look.

[P94]
—It *is* because of you, you bastard.

[P95]
*What was that? I must be hearing things. It definitely wasn’t Sound Transmission.*

[P96]
I tilted my head at the strange phenomenon, then asked, “The grand council isn’t over, is it?”

[P97]
“The grand council runs for three days, alongside the festival. You were told that before you attended.”

[P98]
“I was. Just checking.”

[P99]
The Beast Miao King shook his head at my shameless answer.

[P100]
“Did you really have to take it that far?”

[P101]
“It felt too suspicious to let it go. I wanted to see his real reaction, too.”

[P102]
“That curiosity has made enemies of more than ten thousand Bai people. Add Yohi and Heugung, the two great chieftains who follow Baeksang, and the others, and it would be no exaggeration to say that half of Nanman is against you.”

[P103]
*Hmm. Half of Nanman.*

[P104]
“That’s not as bad as I expected.”

[P105]
“What?”

[P106]
“Two days ago, all of Nanman was against me. I was about to get thrown out before the grand council even started.”

[P107]
“…Hah.”

[P108]
The Beast Miao King gave a hollow laugh and turned to the chieftains who remained.

[P109]
“Chief Jang. Chief Go.”

[P110]
“Yes.”

[P111]
“I need your help. Gather a scouting party of swift warriors and have them watch the approaches from Guizhou.”

[P112]
“Because of the Blood Monk?”

[P113]
The Beast Miao King nodded.

[P114]
“Both Baeksang and Jin Taekyung have a point. The man has no particular reason to come to Nanman. But if he belongs to Dark Heaven, we should be prepared.”

[P115]
“We will obey your command, Palace Lord.”

[P116]
“As you command.”

[P117]
If the chieftains who had left were Baeksang’s people, most of those still here were loyal to the Beast Miao King or were moderates favorably disposed toward him.

[P118]
The two chiefs, each the leader of a mid-sized tribe, accepted their orders without protest. The Beast Miao King’s expression eased a little.

[P119]
“Tonight, we will erect a memorial for those who died and hold a banquet in their honor. The grand council will resume afterward. You may withdraw for now.”

[P120]
* * *

[P121]
“What happened?”

[P122]
Namho came rushing over the moment we returned to our quarters.

[P123]
“You didn’t cause another incident, did you?”

[P124]
His voice brimmed with suspicion. I was about to answer when Hyuk Mujin burst out indignantly.

[P125]
“Old man Nam! What do you take our Captain for?”

[P126]
“What else? A lunatic.”

[P127]
“Now, now. Even if our Captain *is* a lunatic, that’s going too far! Do you seriously think he’d cause trouble at a meeting that important?”

[P128]
“Yes. Easily.”

[P129]
*Is it normal to feel guilty right now?*

[P130]
I hesitated, then opened my mouth. Or tried to.

[P131]
That was when Ju Hwaran joined in.

[P132]
“Elder Namho, that’s too harsh. How can you call our Pavilion Master a lunatic?”

[P133]
If Taishan was the reason Namho was aging so quickly, Ju Hwaran was his one weakness. The man who had been so sure of himself a moment ago scratched his thinning crown.

[P134]
“Well, I…”

[P135]
“Our Pavilion Master came here representing the Murim Alliance. He can be a little rough around the edges, but he knows how important it is to secure Nanman’s entry into the alliance. He would never cause a disturbance at the grand council.”

[P136]
“…”

[P137]
*Please kill me.*

[P138]
My conscience had gone past pricking me. It hurt.

[P139]
Meanwhile, Ju Hwaran was canvassing the others like an enthusiastic campaigner.

[P140]
“What do you all think? Why isn’t anyone answering?”

[P141]
The usually quiet Song Ilseom smacked his lips.

[P142]
“Hmm. Young Bureau Head, perhaps we ought to hear from the man himself first…”

[P143]
“Extra bonus.”

[P144]
“On second thought, you’re right. The Pavilion Master would never do such a thing.”

[P145]
*Money-crazed bastard—out.*

[P146]
“Why aren’t the other two saying anything?”

[P147]
“Taishan. Hungry…”

[P148]
“I heard there’s a banquet tonight.”

[P149]
“Taishan. Strongly agrees with Young Lady Ju.”

[P150]
“…I agree as well.”

[P151]
*Glutton—out. Ex-fiancé I could chew to bits and still not feel satisfied—out.*

[P152]
Her petition gathered signatures with the speed of Quick Attack. Then Ju Hwaran turned eyes sparkling like the Milky Way on me.

[P153]
“Pavilion Master, say something. Did they agree to join the alliance?”

[P154]
One second felt like an hour.

[P155]
After a long silence, I spoke.

[P156]
“Um. Everyone. Well. There was… a minor problem.”

[P157]
Ju Hwaran froze. Namho nodded as if he’d known all along.

[P158]
“See? Crazy Pavilion Master.”

[P159]
“…”

[P160]
“Did you kill someone?”

[P161]
“No.”

[P162]
“Then you hit someone.”

[P163]
“…”

[P164]
“Who? Some chieftain who picked a fight without knowing better? Or someone who said something you didn’t like? Surely not the great chieftain of the Bai people.”

[P165]
“Ah.”

[P166]
“Pavilion Master?”

[P167]
“…”

[P168]
“…Pavilion Master?”

[P169]
As Ju Hwaran’s voice grew faint, I kept my mouth shut and stared toward a distant mountain.

[P170]
Namho chuckled.

[P171]
“See? Crazy bastard.”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.

Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
